newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt rallies strongly across curve at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt rallies strongly across curve at close.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 93.08 (PREV 92.84) 90-DAYS 7.01 (PREV 7.14)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.90 PCT (PREV 6.95) US 5-YR 6.46 (PREV 6.45)
NZ MCI -0.75 vs -1.01
* NZ monetary conditions tighten as TWI rises, rates fall
* Bonds boosted by Asian buying, Australian data
* Govt 02/01 bonds yield 7.026 pct at tender
New Zealand debt rallied sharply to close stronger across the curve on Thursday, as a range of factors acted to boost the market.
A bid tone was evident from the open, as the short-end was bolstered by a higher currency Trade-Weighted Index (TWI), and bonds received a fillip from two eurokiwis issued overnight.
"Then for some reason there was a bit of a feeding frenzy from the Asians -- they came in and started to buy some short bonds -- 98s, 2000s and a few 01s," one dealer said.
He said locals were initially happy to sell some stock as yields were eight to nine basis points stronger, but surprisingly weak Australian employment numbers soon put paid to that inclination.
Australia's seasonally adjusted estimate of the number of employed people fell 40,300 in May to 8.38 million, whereas economists had expected a rise of around 15,000.
"That data was obviously considerably weaker than expectations, and that just caused the local market to buy," the Wellington dealer said.
The 90-day bank bills ended 13 basis points stronger at 7.01 percent, while the front futures contract shot up 24 points to 93.08.
The 02/01 bond ended 18 pips stronger at 6.90 percent, while the long bond rallied 12 to 7.17 percent.
A government tender of NZ$100 million of February 2001 bonds was well supported and yielded 7.026 percent, which was roughly in line with market levels at the time.
Monetary conditions tightened considerably on the day as the TWI, which is very sensitive to the yen, climbed to 67.62 from 67.12 at Wednesday's close.

The U.S. dollar surged against the yen after senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara told reporters Japan would take decisive action to counter excessive swings in foreign exchange rates. The dollar rocketed by more than four yen from its overnight levels in New York after the remarks.

The Reuters Monetary Conditions Index NZ/MCI showed the higher TWI roping conditions in to 75 basis points (in interest rate terms) easier than the Reserve Bank's assumptions, compared with 101 basis points too easy at Wednesday's finish.
-- Catherine McCaw, Wellington newsroom (64 4) 471 4275
